turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_supercon_data.csv: 300 real samples,
column `composition` (element fractions as a compact formula string) and
column `target` (the measured critical temperature Tc (K)).

observed range, that MAXIMIZES critical temperature Tc (K) AND stays robust

any single variable (seek a broad optimum, not a sharp peak). Design
variables:

turns.answer_text:
From the training data, the high-Tc region is overwhelmingly the layered cuprate region. The strongest relevant samples among the requested variables are Ba/Sr/Ca/Cu/O-rich cuprates, e.g. the top non-H/S entry `Hg1Ba2Ca2Cu3O8` at 132 K and the design-variable-only `Ba2Ca2Cu3O` at 126 K. Nearby Tl/Pb/Ba/Sr/Ca/Cu/O compositions also remain very high, around 117–120 K, suggesting this is a broader high-Tc basin rather than a single isolated point.

I would therefore avoid the lower-Tc families in the data: Fe/As pnictides, Nb alloys, MgB2, and substitutions such as Pr/Zn/Ni/Fe that often depress cuprate Tc. I would also avoid chasing the 185 K `H2S` point because H and S are not among the design variables, so that would be an invalid extrapolation in this design space.

A robust choice is a Ba–Sr–Ca–Cu–O cuprate-like composition, slightly Sr/Pb mixed and centered near the high-Tc Ba/Ca/Cu/O cluster rather than exactly on a single sharp sample. In formula-ratio terms, the proposed fractions correspond roughly to:

`Pb0.20Ba1.76Sr0.28Ca1.92Cu2.84O`

with all other listed elements set to zero.
